summary: Nancy Grace Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas, Michael Hahn, and Somadeva Vasudeva.

Nancy Hock is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD in 1987 from the University of California, Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams, and held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco in 1987.

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held an attested post at the University of Delaware in 1997.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indologist and archaeologist. In 1931, he was appointed Superintendent in the Archaeological Survey of India, and he served as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

Naoji Okuyama (b. 1956) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), he taught there (~1985–1993) and subsequently served as a professor at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).
Naoki Nabeshima specializes in Buddhist studies. As attested in 2004, he founded Ryukoku University, where he served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies.
Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) under doctoral supervisor Toshifumi Goto. She later served as a special researcher at Tohoku University.

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, held a fellowship at Cardiff University, and taught at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).
Naomichi Nakada (b. 1928) is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya and under doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and later became director of Toyo Bunko in 1974.

Naoya Funahashi (b. 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and held a post at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo, he served as Superior of Vajirarama in Colombo from around 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (b. 1924) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1971).
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indologist. He served as librarian at Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and later as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested in 1970 and 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Nariaki Nakazato (b. 1946) is a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1984–2010) and also held posts at Toyo Bunko and Kobe University.
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, with posts attested in 1974 and 1988.
